_meta.document: OpenAI Agentic Commerce product feed - INTERNAL DRAFT
_meta.do_not_submit_reason: Two blockers: (1) price and availability are unresolved and there is no implemented Amazon offer source; (2) image_url is WebP and the spec requires a direct JPEG or PNG link. See commerce/platform-readiness.md.
_meta.target_feed_format: JSONL (one record per line). This file is pretty-printed JSON for review only; the emitted feed must be JSONL.

record.title: JUMVI Toss & Catch Game Set - 4 Hand-Strap Paddles, 4 Sticky Balls, 36 Guided Missions, Ages 3-12
record.description: JUMVI Toss & Catch is a 2-4 player toss-and-catch activity set for ages 3-12. The box contains 4 hand-strap EVA paddles, 4 sticky toss-and-catch balls, a mesh carry bag and a QR Mission Card. Scanning the QR Mission Card opens the JUMVI Mission Hub in a mobile browser with 36 Guided Missions across 6 skill packs. No app download and no signup are required.
record.product_category: Toys & Games > Outdoor Play > Toss & Catch Games

_field_notes.item_id: Stable neutral internal ID. Per spec, item_id must stay stable and must never be reused. No better-established internal ID exists in the repository.
_field_notes.title: 97 characters, within the 150-character limit. Front-loads brand and product type, then the verified contents and age range. No superlatives or promotional padding.
_field_notes.description: Plain factual text, 358 characters, well within the 5,000-character limit. Every claim traces to a verified field in product-truth.json.
_field_notes.url: The canonical homepage. jumvi.co has no product-detail route; the homepage IS the product page.
_field_notes.seller_name: SAY23 LLC is the brand owner and seller of record. This is not the marketplace name - see _marketplace_position below.
_field_notes.image_url: UNRESOLVED. product-truth.json media is WebP; the spec requires a direct JPEG or PNG link. A JPEG or PNG derivative of assets/v5-hero-action.webp must be produced and published first.
_field_notes.availability: UNRESOLVED by design. A live Amazon offer fact. Must be filled at build time from dynamic_offer_facts.source_interfaces.amazon_offer_source, using one of in_stock / out_of_stock / pre_order / backorder / unknown.
_field_notes.price: UNRESOLVED by design. A live Amazon offer fact. Must be filled at build time in the spec's money format, '<amount> <CURRENCY>' e.g. '29.99 USD'. Never hardcode, never reuse a cached value.
_field_notes.gtin: Omitted. No GTIN is verified. The spec validates the check digit, and an invented value would fail validation as well as being a false identity claim.
_field_notes.review_count: Omitted. Recommended by the spec for discovery, but JUMVI has no first-party review corpus. Amazon review data belongs to Amazon and is not republished.
_field_notes.sku_mpn: The spec has no sku or mpn field, so no mapping is emitted. Even if a compatible field existed, JUMVI-001 and JMV-TC-001 remain unresolved and must not be mapped - see identifiers.unresolved in product-truth.json.
_field_notes.is_eligible_search: Set true to request search/discovery eligibility. The spec documents this as a request flag that defaults to true; it is NOT a guarantee of display, ranking or inclusion. OpenAI makes no documented promise about visibility or placement.
_field_notes.is_eligible_checkout: Set false. Checkout happens on Amazon, not on jumvi.co. Setting this true requires a completed OpenAI checkout integration (Agentic Checkout / Instant Checkout) that this project does not have.
_field_notes.seller_tos: UNRESOLVED. jumvi.co publishes a privacy policy but no terms of service page. The spec lists seller_tos as required for checkout; it is not required for search-only eligibility.

_marketplace_position.situation: The physical product is sold on Amazon US (ASIN B0H16JPQCF). jumvi.co is a brand and product-information site with no cart and no checkout.
_marketplace_position.finding: The published OpenAI product feed specification does NOT define a marketplace_seller field, and the commerce documentation contains no explicit marketplace, third-party-seller, multi-seller or reseller support. Its seller fields are written for a single merchant that both lists and fulfils. This was checked against the feed spec and the consolidated commerce docs on 2026-09-12.
_marketplace_position.consequence: There is no field to add that would correctly express 'listed by SAY23 LLC, transacted on Amazon'. Adding an invented marketplace_seller column would fabricate support that the spec does not document.
_marketplace_position.decision: No marketplace field is emitted. Marketplace/third-party-seller handling must be confirmed directly with OpenAI during merchant onboarding, and any marketplace representation must follow whatever the feed-specific setup they provide actually specifies.
_marketplace_position.open_question_for_openai: Does the programme accept a discovery-only feed from a brand whose checkout is on a third-party marketplace, and if so how should the marketplace and the seller of record be represented?
